newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Marieberg sells half of Duni to SEP.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Marieberg sells half of Duni to SEP.

text.p: Swedish media group Tidnings AB Marieberg said on Thursday it signed an agreement with Scandinavian Equity Partners Limited (SEP) for SEP to become half-owner of disposable tableware maker Duni AB.
At present Duni is a wholly owned subsidiary of Marieberg.
Marieberg's shares were suspended on the Stockholm bourse on Thursday morning at the initiative of the company and bourse.
The company is due to report interim results on Thursday.
Marieberg said in a statement the Duni transaction was estimated to bring a windfall gain of about one billion Swedish crowns ($150.9 million).
Duni is a leader in the Swedish tableware market, with a 1995 turnover of 5.24 billion crowns and operating profit after depreciation of 369 million crowns.

SEP, created in 1994 by Investor AB and AEA Investors Inc of the U.S., is an active shareholder in medium-sized Nordic companies with the potential for development and growth, Marieberg said. ($ = 6.626 Swedish Crowns)
